claims.text: The trip was booked on an upfront quote of SGD 12.90 (fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd) but the ledger records charged_total of SGD 16.10, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The SGD 3.20 gap is absorbed by no pass-through or statutory line: tolls/ERP are SGD 0.00, the airport surcharge is SGD 0.00 and waiting_time_fee is SGD 0.00. Under POL-RD-11(a) the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 is refunded in full, and that amount is SGD 3.20.

Because fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null, POL-RD-11 fixed the distance and time charges at booking and closed the POL-RD-02 recomputation route altogether. The rider's loss on this trip is therefore not a distance or time loss that the billed mileage can answer; it is the difference between the quote and the total actually charged. The only question POL-RD-11 leaves open is whether a properly chargeable pass-through line absorbs that difference, and on this artifact none does.

The rider does not need a route deviation to succeed, and I do not overstate one: the trace shows the trip ran 3.37 km against a booked optimal of 3.3 km, an excess of 0.07 km or 2.12%, so neither POL-RD-01 gate is met (greater than 0.8 km absolute and greater than 20% of optimal). That concession cuts against the driver, not the rider — if the trip did not deviate, the SGD 3.20 over the quote cannot be defended as a distance charge, and under POL-RD-11 the rider's remedy does not depend on the excess at all.

The driver's only explanation is 'there was some traffic at the last junction'. No traffic advisory for this corridor is in the pool: EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING, its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so I disclose that this claim rests on an artifact of zero weight — the absence is itself citable. No POL-RD-03 exoneration can be run, because an advisory that does not exist can name no road, carry no validity window and supply no shortest lawful alternative. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden.

The fare_breakdown's own rate card does not reproduce the component lines it charges. At per_km_rate_sgd 0.75, 3.4 km yields 2.55, yet distance_fare is recorded at 5.07; at per_min_rate_sgd 0.28, 13.0 minutes yields 3.64, yet time_fare is recorded at 6.43 — with surge_multiplier at 1.0 and surge_amount at 0.00. Nothing on the artifact bridges that gap, so the record supplies no rate-card basis for charging the rider SGD 3.20 more than the SGD 12.90 he was quoted.

The GPS artifact is complete and unimpaired: 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence against an expected 10-second interval, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0 across the whole trip. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs therefore do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged, so this dispute can be decided on the record and the contested SGD 3.20 refunded rather than held — escalation would only suspend money that the fare ledger already shows is owed.

The rider says the fare 'went back to 12.90' the moment the dispute was pressed, but the ledger does not bear that out: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the SGD 3.20 has not in fact been returned. I do not rely on the rider's recollection where the artifact contradicts it. The present state stands against the rider, and under POL-GEN-03 only an affirmative PARTIAL_REFUND of that SGD 3.20 under POL-RD-11(a) will move the money.

claims.text: The governing measurement is this trip's own GPS trace, and it records 3.37 km driven against a platform optimal route of 3.3 km - an excess of 0.07 km, or 2.12%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail: 2.12% is nowhere near the 20% relative gate and 0.07 km is nowhere near the 0.8 km absolute gate, and the derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. On the trip's own trace, no route deviation is established against this driver.

That no-deviation finding rests on a trace that is clean for policy purposes: 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage 100%, an empty gaps list and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires - there is no >90 s gap, no >500 m jump and no sampling interval above 30 s - so the excess is measured from the trace itself and needs no surrogate, and the measurement is reliable.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the price was fixed at booking, with quoted_fare_sgd of 12.90 on the ledger and a rate card of RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEX. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess may be. The rider's theory - that a trip which ran a little long should cost more - has no route-deviation refund behind it, and the fare was set by the platform, not by the driver.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08: before anything shifts to the driver, the rider must cite evidence showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trace shows no such excess, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the claim fails on the rider's own evidence.

No repeat-deviation pattern is available against this driver. His trailing-90-day record shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, so neither the 3-flag limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb of POL-RD-06 is satisfied. POL-RD-06 is not even engaged, because it is triggered only by a material deviation and none has been found, so no uplift and no conduct referral follows.

There is no billing-integrity defect to lay at the driver's door: every pass-through and statutory line is zero - tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and an ERP-lines total of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates at an airport nor crosses a charged gantry. There is therefore no unmatched gantry and no misapplied surcharge for POL-RD-09 to correct.

This is a rider-filed dispute, and under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling leaves the present payment state standing rather than restoring or reversing anything. The ledger shows that present state to be payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider's assertion that the fare 'went back to 12.90' the moment he pressed dispute is simply not in the record. The charge the driver earned stands, and the outcome the evidence supports is NO_ACTION.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the two of you actually agree on most of the facts, and the case turns on a rule the driver's side did not address.

Agreed and accepted. No route deviation is established. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00524) records 3.37 km driven against the platform's booked optimal of 3.3 km (EV-TRIP-00524) — an excess of 0.07 km, or 2.12% — which is below both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal). The trace is also clean for policy purposes: 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage 100%, an empty gaps list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07 does not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Because no material deviation exists, POL-RD-06 is not triggered (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, neither limb met), so there is no conduct referral and no driver compensation. The rider also fairly concedes that the trace shows no deviation, and I accept that concession against his own interest. Every pass-through line is zero (tolls/ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00, ERP-lines total 0.00), so there is no phantom gantry or misapplied surcharge and nothing for POL-RD-09(4) to refer.

The driver's traffic assertion. The statement that 'there was some traffic at the last junction' is a general assertion that cites no advisory and no evidence ID; EV-ADVIS-00524-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), and POL-RD-08 gives a bare assertion of bad traffic no weight. No POL-RD-03 exoneration can run against a non-existent advisory. This does not change the outcome, because nothing needs exonerating where no deviation has been established.

Where the driver's case fails. The driver is right that this is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip (EV-FARE-00524) and that under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large any excess might be. That part is accepted. But the conclusion of NO_ACTION does not follow, because POL-RD-11(a) is an independent remedy the driver's case never addresses. The ledger records a quote of SGD 12.90 (quoted_fare_sgd) against a charged total of SGD 16.10 (charged_total), with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The gap of SGD 3.20 is absorbed by no properly chargeable pass-through or statutory line — tolls/ERP 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 — so under POL-RD-11(a) it is refunded in full: 16.10 − 12.90 = 3.20. The driver's argument that the fare was set by the app, not by him, is accepted as to liability but does not defeat a refund of a charge the ledger itself shows exceeded the fixed price.

The rider's two further points. First, the assertion that the fare 'went back to 12.90' the moment the dispute was pressed is not borne out by the ledger — payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 — and is not relied on. Second, the point that the fare breakdown's own component lines do not reproduce its rate card (at 0.75/km and 0.28/min, 3.4 km and 13.0 min yield 2.55 and 3.64, not the recorded distance_fare 5.07 and time_fare 6.43, with surge_multiplier 1.0) does not alter the amount owed, which POL-RD-11(a) fixes by the quote-versus-total comparison, but the platform should reconcile those lines.

Outcome. The quoted price of SGD 12.90 stands as the amount properly chargeable, plus zero pass-throughs. The rider is refunded the SGD 3.20 by which the SGD 16.10 charged exceeded the SGD 12.90 quote, and the contested amount is otherwise left in place. The USD/GPS, trip and fare records all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00524, so no escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires and this case is decided rather than held.

Confidence 0.90: the deciding figures (quoted_fare_sgd 12.90 and charged_total 16.10) are carried by EV-FARE-00524 at weight_multiplier 1.0, which is the cap.

At per_km_rate_sgd 0.75, 3.4 km yields 2.55, yet distance_fare is recorded at 5.07; at per_min_rate_sgd 0.28, 13.0 minutes yields 3.64, yet time_fare is recorded at 6.43 — with surge_multiplier at 1.0 and surge_amount at 0.00. Nothing on the artifact bridges that gap, so the record supplies no rate-card basis for charging the rider SGD 3.20 more than the SGD 12.90 he was quoted.

The GPS artifact is complete and unimpaired: 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence against an expected 10-second interval, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec 0.0 across the whole trip. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs therefore do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged, so this dispute can be decided on the record and the contested SGD 3.20 refunded rather than held — escalation would only suspend money that the fare ledger already shows is owed.

The rider says the fare 'went back to 12.90' the moment the dispute was pressed, but the ledger does not bear that out: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the SGD 3.20 has not in fact been returned. I do not rely on the rider's recollection where the artifact contradicts it. The present state stands against the rider, and under POL-GEN-03 only an affirmative PARTIAL_REFUND of that SGD 3.20 under POL-RD-11(a) will move the money.

The governing measurement is this trip's own GPS trace, and it records 3.37 km driven against a platform optimal route of 3.3 km - an excess of 0.07 km, or 2.12%. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests fail: 2.12% is nowhere near the 20% relative gate and 0.07 km is nowhere near the 0.8 km absolute gate, and the derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. On the trip's own trace, no route deviation is established against this driver.

That no-deviation finding rests on a trace that is clean for policy purposes: 79 fixes at a 10-second cadence, coverage 100%, an empty gaps list and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires - there is no >90 s gap, no >500 m jump and no sampling interval above 30 s - so the excess is measured from the trace itself and needs no surrogate, and the measurement is reliable.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: the price was fixed at booking, with quoted_fare_sgd of 12.90 on the ledger and a rate card of RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEX. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess may be. The rider's theory - that a trip which ran a little long should cost more - has no route-deviation refund behind it, and the fare was set by the platform, not by the driver.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08: before anything shifts to the driver, the rider must cite evidence showing an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trace shows no such excess, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the claim fails on the rider's own evidence.

No repeat-deviation pattern is available against this driver. His trailing-90-day record shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, so neither the 3-flag limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb of POL-RD-06 is satisfied. POL-RD-06 is not even engaged, because it is triggered only by a material deviation and none has been found, so no uplift and no conduct referral follows.

There is no billing-integrity defect to lay at the driver's door: every pass-through and statutory line is zero - tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and an ERP-lines total of 0.00 on a trip that neither originates at an airport nor crosses a charged gantry. There is therefore no unmatched gantry and no misapplied surcharge for POL-RD-09 to correct.

This is a rider-filed dispute, and under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling leaves the present payment state standing rather than restoring or reversing anything. The ledger shows that present state to be payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider's assertion that the fare 'went back to 12.90' the moment he pressed dispute is simply not in the record. The charge the driver earned stands, and the outcome the evidence supports is NO_ACTION.
